name: Bantang
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Kitjapol Udomkool. 2006. A phonological comparison of selected Phunoi varieties (incl. Ban Tang). MA thesis, Payap University (cited on Glottolog; thesis not found online).

sources.citation: Ferlus, Michel. 2019. Lexique phounoy-français (HAL halshs-02188910); Ferlus 1980 Le verbe en phounoy (CLAO 8); Bradley 1977 Phunoi or Côông (PL A-49).
sources.note: Phunoi proper (Phongsaly), not Bantang; none of the three mentions Bantang/Ban Tang and none states a stress rule (per the phun1245 audit and grep).

sources.citation: Kitjapol Udomkool. 2006. A phonological comparison of selected Bisoid speech varieties. MA thesis, Payap University, Chiang Mai. 207 pp. (Bantang phonology §3.1, pp. 45-67.)
sources.note: Nothing. The Bantang chapter covers syllable structure (CV, CVC, CVV, CVVC), consonants, clusters, vowels, diphthongs and three tones (35/33/31, pp. 65-67) with tone distribution by syllable position; grep stress|accent|prominence|intonation|pitch = 0 hits in the whole thesis. Only word-level prosodic remark: low tone never occurs word-finally, 'there may be a word level phonological process occurring' (p. 67). Bantang data = Sue Wright's wordlist recordings retranscribed by the author (p. 35).

sources.citation: Edmondson, Jerold A. 2005. The Central and Southern Loloish languages of Vietnam. Proceedings of BLS 28, Special Session on Tibeto-Burman and Southeast Asian Linguistics, 1-13.
sources.note: No mention of Bantang/Ban Tang at all (grep of text and scanned layers); its stress remarks concern Côông of Vietnam (first syllable often unstressed, iambic) and Phunoi minor syllables, not Bantang.

sources.citation: Roux, Henri. 1924. Deux tribus de la région de Phongsaly (Laos septentrional). BEFEO 24: 373-500.
sources.note: Nothing; 'Ban Tang' appears only as a P'u Noi village name in the Phya Khattya village group list. Ethnographic; no linguistic description of the Ban Tang variety.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid record bant1298 (Hammarström et al.), with reference records 472988, 719149, 552659, 309627, 311111.
sources.note: Nothing; lists Kitjapol 2006 (phonology, 28 pp. on Bantang) and Wright 2003 (wordlist) as the most extensive descriptions, plus Lama 2012 and Edmondson 2005 for classification. Ethnologue comment: Ban Tang not inherently intelligible to Phunoi (citing Udomkool 2006: 42 and Wright).
Nothing beyond the autonym with tone numbers (ban33 taŋ33); cites Udomkool 2006 and Wright n.d. manuscript.

sources.citation: Dai Qingxia 戴庆厦 et al. 2018. 老挝普内语研究 [A study of Phunoi in Laos]. Beijing: China Social Sciences Press.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Modern full description of a Laos Phunoi variety by a Chinese team; Chinese-academy grammars usually have a 重音 (stress) note. Describes Phunoi proper, not Bantang, so at best a proxy for the cluster.

sources.citation: Lama, Ziwo Qiu-Fuyuan. 2012. Subgrouping of Nisoic (Yi) languages. PhD dissertation, University of Texas at Arlington. 399 pp.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Cited by Glottolog for Bantang; comparative, uses Kitjapol's Bantang data; could confirm whether any prosodic (minor-syllable/stress) characterisation of Bantang exists in the literature. Low chance of a stress rule.

sources.citation: Wright, Pamela Sue. 2003. Singsali (Phunoi) Speech Varieties of Phongsali Province. Language and Life Journal 1: 62-73 (Vientiane).
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only other primary source on Bantang (the survey whose wordlist recordings underlie Kitjapol's Bantang chapter); might carry transcription notes on prosody, though Glottolog types it a wordlist/overview so a stress statement is unlikely.
